contentCheck.notes: Crop shows the thermodynamic data table for reactions X, Y, Z and parts (a)-(f)(iii); matches page. Catalog parts a–c, d, e–f refined into a, b, c, d, e, f-i, f-ii, f-iii as printed.

primary.evidence: Must write Kp for C(s) + H2O(g) <=> CO(g) + H2(g), omitting the solid carbon.
Must use ΔH° = +131 kJ/mol (endothermic) to predict that raising the temperature shifts reaction X toward products and increases Kp.
Must relate the positive ΔG°298 = +29 kJ/mol for reaction Y to Kp being less than 1.
Must reason from ΔH° = +41 kJ/mol that more energy is absorbed breaking reactant bonds than is released forming product bonds, so compare total bond energies.
Must argue that ΔH°, ΔS° and ΔG° values give no information about reaction rate, which depends on activation energy.
Must predict the sign of ΔS° for 2 CO(g) -> C(s) + CO2(g) from the decrease in moles of gas.
Must recognize reaction Z is the reverse of the sum of X and Y and combine their ΔH° values accordingly.
Must determine that ΔG° for reaction Z (from reversing and summing X and Y, or from its ΔH° and ΔS°) is negative, so CO(g) converts to C(s) and CO2(g).

supporting.evidence: Must reason that converting 2 mol gas to 1 mol gas at constant volume and temperature lowers the pressure.

uncertainty: Part (f)(iii) requires combining ΔG° values of reactions by state-function addition; no concept covers ΔG/ΔS manipulation (hess-law is ΔH only), so it is folded into gibbs-free-energy.
